title: Threadgill's 29 points and Jallow's all-around brilliance clinch BOV League D1 title for Starlites in decisive Game 5
description: Starlites Naxxar captured the 2025-26 BOV League Division I championship on Sunday, pulling away from Depiro 98-77 in a decisive Game 5 at the Ta' Qali Basketball Pavilion to win the best-of-five finals 3-2 and claim the Maltese men's title. After the two sides had traded blows across four tightly contested games to reach a 2-2 deadlock, the decider was anything but tight. Starlites exploded offensively, shooting a blistering 50.8 percent from the field (32-of-63), converting 28-of-33 free throws (84.8%), and racking up 24 assists as their ball movement overwhelmed Depiro's defense in the biggest game of the season.
imageCaption: Hibernians clinch title in Game 5 decider (Photo: Hibs)

title: Hibernians capture BOV League D1 trophy
description: Hibernians - Luxol 93-83 Hibernians celebrated BOV League D1 title. They outgunned Luxol in Game 4 of the Finals to conquer the trophy. American swingman Tedrick Wolfe (196-1997, college: Wayland Baptist) fired 35 points (!!!) and 8 rebounds for the winners. Canadian-Ghanian point guard James Agyeman (178-1994) chipped in 18 points, 7 rebounds and 8 assists. Wolfe is a former Eurobasket Summer League player, which is considered top international summer league in the market. Hibernians' coach used an eleven-player rotation which allowed the starters a little rest for the next games. American forward Caleb Jones-McCrary (203-2000, college: MNU) produced a double-double by scoring 29 points, 20 rebounds and 4 assists (on 13-of-17 shooting from the field) and international Nathan Xuereb (180-2001) added 18 points and 4 steals respectively for lost side.
imageCaption: Hibernians capture BOV League D1 trophy (Photo: instagram)

title: BOV League D1 Round 3 of Finals. Starlites clinch the title
description: Starlites - Mellieha 100-89 Starlites clinched BOV League D1 title. They held off Mellieha in Game 3 of the Finals to complete the sweep. It was a great evening for the former international point guard Alec Pace (178-1998) who led his team to a victory scoring 24 points and 6 assists. American Davonte Craven (203-1999, college: Rust) helped adding 21 points and 6 rebounds. The best for the losing side was American swingman Tedrick Wolfe (196-1997, college: Wayland Baptist) with 28 points, 5 rebounds and 4 assists and the former international David Bugeja (180-1992) scored 15 points and 8 rebounds. Five Mellieha players scored in double figures.

title: Starlites claim League title
description: Mellieha - Starlites 91-113 Starlites conquered the BOV National League title. They fired past Mellieha in Game 3 of the title series to complete the sweep. Alec Pace (178-PG-1998) and Zekiah Owens (197-G/F-1998, college: AIC) posted 28 points each for the champions. Starlites sank 28 points in the first period to take a 10-point lead. Mellieha cut the deficit in the second term as they trailed by 7 points at halftime 39-46. But Starlites drained 38 points in the third term to boost the lead back to double-digits. They added 29 points in the fourth quarter and rallied to the win. Darius George (201-F, college: Marshall) finished with 25 points for Starlites. Vukasin Jandric answered with 23 points and 11 rebounds, while David Bugeja (180-SG-1992) had 22 points in the loss.

title: Starlites Fijo win Division One championship
description: Starlites Basketball Club are the BOV Basketball First Division League champions for 2021-22. Starlites led the standings all the way to the play-off final, where they beat Melliea Libertas Spalding 3-0 in the best-of-five play-off final. Charles Azzopardi, Head CSR at Bank of Valletta, accompanied by Paul Sultana, President of the Malta Basketball Association presented the BOV Basketball First Division League Trophy to the new champions. Alec Felice Pace (178-PG-1998) was selected as the Most Valuable Player of the Playoff Final and presented with a commemorative plaque. In a statement, Bank of Valletta said its support of Maltese Basketball can be traced back to the 1980s as part of the bank's active role within the community in which it operates as part of its Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) commitment.
imageCaption: Starlites Fijo win Division One championship (Photo: Facebook)

title: All senior leagues and cup finals cancelled
description: Following an urgent Council meeting held this evening, the local basketball clubs agreed, with great regret after that all the sacrifices they made along the season were seemingly totally disregarded, to cancel the senior leagues for this season, namely the BOV Men First Division, the MAPFRE MSV Life Women League as well as the BOV Amateur Men League together with the finals of the BOV Knock Out Men in both the senior men categories. The general feeling, as discussed amongst the clubs this evening, was one of great lamentation and disappointment as each had made considerable efforts to safeguard all those involved whilst having to bear extra financial costs to ensure a safe playing environment and adopting a stringent COVID-19 protocol as well as compulsory swab tests for all players and officials ahead of every game.
